purpose: Test whether the existing foreground-occupancy-trained CBAM channel gate ranks the previously frozen random 1024-key groups by their measured local deletion utility. Reuse saved source features; no additional video propagation or model training.
scope: Use the existing development seq2/3/4 and sequence-separated validation seq9/10 fixed-read results. All these data and prior results have been inspected; this is an exploratory diagnostic, not independent confirmation. Only eligible labeled-present reads permit Dice utility. Empty-frame outcomes remain a separate safety observation, not a Dice ranking.
score: For each source frame in a verified read, compute prompt-conditioned existing CBAM gate scores, unweighted early-FPN foreground-minus-background contrast, and RGB foreground-minus-background contrast using the automatic initialization prompt. Map each saved memory key to the verified 64x64 spatial token ID, and average the source scores over each frozen deletion group. Include per-source deterministically shuffled unweighted scores and mean source-frame age as nonsemantic controls. Construct all scores before opening deletion outcomes; no label information enters descriptors.
target: After scores are frozen, utility is no-op Dice minus group-deletion Dice: positive means the group helped that particular frozen read. Evaluate within-read pairwise ranking concordance, count ties as half and exclude tied utility pairs. Report individual reads, sequence means and number of tied pairs, with no tuning or checkpoint selection on validation. Group effects are conditional, near zero, correlated within reads, and do not establish online ranking or full-video benefit.
limitations: The existing gate was trained to predict foreground occupancy, not deletion utility, and development sequences overlap that training. Seq9/10 were used for prior model assessment, so neither split is an untouched test. Random-group means can dilute local features. The Lean historical usage-rank control is unavailable in these snapshots; current-read attention stats would require first performing the full read and must not be called a pre-read usage baseline. Existing matched usage and distributed controls remain separately reported in the priority fixed-read study. No untrained attention weights, detector reruns, redetection, threshold or GT-derived inference signal.
